newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen futures lower in sympathy with JGBs.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen futures lower in sympathy with JGBs.

text.p: Key September Euroyen futures ended Thursday's TIFFE day session down in line with Japanese government bond (JGB) futures.
The September settled at 99.24, after falling as low as 99.22. The volume was 56,042 contracts.
"Following a fall in JGB futures, Euroyen futures were pushed lower by liquidation of long positions," said a brokerage house trader.
Key March JGB futures closed down 0.35 at 124.95, after falling as low as 124.66.

"Compared with JGB futures, Euroyen futures' downside may be limited as Euroyen cash is looking stable. Unless there is a change in the market's perception that the Bank of Japan (BOJ) will maintain its easy credit policy, Euroyen futures are likely to remain well-supported," said a city bank trader.
The stock market's weakness rules out the possibility of any interest rate hike, a trust bank trader said.
Tokyo's Nikkei 225 average closed down 257.83 points or 1.32 percent at 19,291.58.
The key stock index dipped to an intraday low of 18,819.92 in the afternoon.
Players were also focusing on Japan's industrial production data, released after the close of the Euroyen futures' TIFFE day session.
Industrial production fell a preliminary 1.9 percent month-on-month in November, which was within economists' forecast range of minus 1.4 percent to minus 2.1 percent.
Traders do not expect the industrial production data to have an impact on the Euroyen futures market on Friday.
In the interbank money market, key unsecured overnight call money was traded at 0.50 percent, unchanged from Wednesday.
The BOJ drained a net 100 billion yen from the money market in the morning, maintaining a neutral stance.
About 50 billion yen worth of key three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) was issued at 0.52 percent, unchanged from the previous day, traders said.
